merge.label: Merge rules (two profiles of one person)
merge.help: Which matches put two customer profiles on the "To review" list as maybe the same person: the same e-mail, one profile's WhatsApp number being the other's phone, the same name with the same address, or the same identity in the order identity graph (only while that graph is on in Orders › Risk rules). The shop never merges by itself: a person with the merge permission looks at both and presses Merge, or "Not the same person" (then the pair is never suggested again). A merge moves nothing — orders, wallets and notes stay where they are and the first profile's page shows both — and "Split" undoes it exactly. "Per page": how many pairs the list shows at a time. "Note needed": a merge needs a short note (a split always does). Off ("Suggest pairs" off): no suggestions; a person can still merge two profiles by hand.

phoneMask.label: Masked phone numbers
phoneMask.help: A team member without the "full phone number" permission sees customers' numbers masked, with this many digits kept at the start and at the end (3 and 3: 017•••••678). With the permission (you have every permission) the number is shown in full, and every copy and call is logged in "Who looked at this customer".

list.label: Customers list and its views
list.help: How many customers one page of the Customers list shows; how many orders make a customer "Returning" (fewer is "New"); after how many days without an order a customer who already had a delivery shows under "At risk"; and the delivered spend (Sales, delivered orders only) that makes a customer "VIP". The VIP figure is empty as it ships: the VIP view stays hidden until you type your own figure. Nothing here changes a price, COD or an offer; the views only sort who is who.

profile.label: One customer's page
profile.help: How many orders one customer's page lists before "Older"; how many exchanges and support conversations each of its lists shows; and how many lines of "Who looked at this customer" (every open of the page and every copy or call of the full number, with who and when) the owner sees there (0 hides the card; the full log stays). Nothing here changes what is recorded.

segments.label: Saved segments
segments.help: Groups of customers by what they really did (orders, delivered spend, true delivery share, last order, a category or size bought, an area, where they first came from, offers consent, a refusal, an exchange), saved by name and used again in the Customers list and later in campaigns. "On": the Segments page counts and saves; off (as shipped): the page only says it is off. "Most segments": how many saved segments the store may keep (archived ones do not count). "Most conditions": how many conditions one segment joins with “and”. "Shown in the builder": how many matching customers the builder lists beside its live count. A segment never sends anything by itself, and nothing in it moves money or blocks anyone.
